summary.title: Nim Days: Day 4 - Writing a Link Checker
summary.one_liner: Learn to build a link checker in Nim in sequential, async (asyncdispatch), and threaded styles, and compare their run times.
takeaways: A link is treated as valid when its HTTP GET returns status 200; errors are caught with try/except.
Async version uses {.async.} procs, newAsyncHttpClient, yield on futures, and await all(futures) to run requests concurrently.
In the author's run, the sequential checker took about 7.7 seconds and the async version about 3.6 seconds on a slow connection.
Use await only inside async procs and waitFor to call async procs from sync code.
Threaded version uses spawn and FlowVar with the ^ operator; compile with -d:ssl for https.
summary.summary: The author builds a link checker in Nim in three ways: sequential with newHttpClient, asynchronous with asyncdispatch and newAsyncHttpClient, and an extra threaded version using threadpool. Each checker takes a list of links and reports whether each returns HTTP 200. The page includes timing results from the author's own connection, where async finished in about 3.6 seconds versus 7.7 seconds sequentially. It also explains the CLI wrapper that reads links from a file, and notes that nim.cfg needs -d:ssl for https.
